checklist.step: Maintain the covered-establishment register and exemption determinations
actions: Each January, pull the location roster from the HRIS (Workday: Organization ▸ Locations report) with headcount and NAICS code per site.

Apply the 29 CFR 1904.1 size test (company-wide peak employment of 10 or fewer at any point in the prior year exempts routine recordkeeping) and the 1904.2 Appendix A partial-exemption test against each site's NAICS code, noting that an exempt establishment must still keep records if OSHA or BLS notifies it in writing.
Record the covered/exempt call, the NAICS basis and the decision date on the establishment register worksheet.
Route the register to Employment Counsel for written concurrence and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a counsel-concurred establishment register dated this January names every site as covered or exempt with its NAICS basis.

checklist.step: Open the calendar-year Form 300 and 301 set for every covered establishment
actions: Download the current OSHA Forms 300/300A/301 package from osha.gov/recordkeeping/forms or roll forward the approved equivalent workbook.
Create one workbook per covered establishment on the HR Operations SharePoint site named OSHA-300-<establishment>-<year>, with the establishment name, city and state in the Form 300 header.
Carry nothing forward from the prior year — the Form 300 log restarts empty on January 1.
Set workbook permissions so only named recordkeepers can edit and record their names in the register.
checklist.done: every covered establishment has an empty, permissioned current-year 300/301 workbook with a completed header.

checklist.step: Intake every reported injury and illness through the HRIS incident case
actions: When a manager or employee reports an injury or illness, open a safety-incident case in the HRIS capturing: employee name and job title, establishment, date of injury/onset, where it occurred, what the employee was doing, and the injury/illness description.
Attach the first report of injury, any medical note, and the workers' compensation claim number if one was filed.
Confirm the case date-of-knowledge field is the date HR or a supervisor first learned of the case — this starts the 7-calendar-day entry clock under 1904.29(b)(3).
Hand the case to the establishment recordkeeper via HRIS assignment the same business day.
checklist.done: each reported case exists as an HRIS incident with a date-of-knowledge and is assigned to a recordkeeper.

checklist.step: Decide work-relatedness under 29 CFR 1904.5 before anything else
actions: Apply the presumption: an event or exposure in the work environment that caused or contributed to the condition, or significantly aggravated a pre-existing condition, is work-related.

Walk the 1904.5(b)(2) exception list (present as a member of the general public, symptoms merely surfacing at work, voluntary wellness/fitness activity, eating own food, personal grooming, common cold/flu, personal mental illness absent an opinion) and record which, if any, applies.
For telework staff, apply 1904.5(b)(7): record only if the injury occurred while performing work for pay at home and is directly related to the work rather than the home environment.
Write the conclusion and the specific exception relied on into the recordability worksheet attached to the HRIS case.
checklist.done: the case carries a written work-related / not-work-related call citing the exact 1904.5 basis.

checklist.step: Apply the 29 CFR 1904.7 recordability criteria
actions: Mark the case recordable if it involves death, days away from work, restricted work or job transfer, medical treatment beyond first aid, or loss of consciousness.

Check the 1904.7(b)(5)(ii) first-aid list verbatim (non-prescription medication at non-prescription strength, tetanus immunization, cleaning/flushing wounds, bandages/butterfly closures, hot/cold therapy, finger guards, drilling a nail, eye patches, removing foreign bodies by irrigation or cotton swab, drinking fluids for heat stress) — anything on the list is not medical treatment.

Mark recordable any significant injury or illness diagnosed by a physician or other licensed health care professional (cancer, chronic irreversible disease, fractured or cracked bone or tooth, punctured eardrum) even without treatment, per 1904.7(b)(7).
Where two health care professionals differ, record which recommendation was followed and the most authoritative opinion relied on.
checklist.done: the worksheet states recordable or not-recordable with the specific 1904.7 criterion or first-aid list item cited.

checklist.step: Enter recordable cases on the Form 300 log within 7 calendar days
actions: Within 7 calendar days of the date-of-knowledge, add a Form 300 row: case number, employee name, job title, date of injury/onset, where the event occurred, and the injury/illness description with the object/substance involved.
Tick exactly one outcome column — (G) death, (H) days away, (I) job transfer or restriction, or (J) other recordable case — and one injury/illness type column (M1–M6).
Complete the matching OSHA Form 301 incident report (or the equivalent workers' comp first report carrying the same data fields) within the same 7 calendar days.
Record the log-entry date on the HRIS case to stop the SLA timer.
checklist.done: the 300 row and 301 report exist within 7 calendar days of knowledge and the HRIS case shows the entry date.

checklist.step: Handle privacy concern cases per 29 CFR 1904.29(b)(6)-(9)
actions: Classify as a privacy concern case: injury to an intimate body part or reproductive system, sexual assault, mental illness, HIV/hepatitis/tuberculosis, needlestick with contaminated sharp, or any illness the employee independently asks to be kept private.
Enter 'Privacy Case' in the Form 300 name column instead of the employee's name.
Keep the confidential case-number-to-name concordance in a separate restricted-access file, never in the log workbook.
Ask Employment Counsel before releasing any privacy-case detail outside the recordkeeping team.
checklist.done: every qualifying case reads 'Privacy Case' on the log and appears in the restricted concordance.

checklist.step: Count days away and restricted days by the calendar-day rules
actions: Count calendar days — weekends and holidays included — starting the day after the injury or onset, using the HRIS absence records for the employee.
Cap the count at 180 days away and/or restricted per 1904.7(b)(3)(vii) and stop counting when the employee is released to full duty or the count hits the cap.
Where the physician recommends days away that the employee declines, record the recommended days.
Update columns K and L on the Form 300 row as the counts grow, and reclassify the outcome column if the case worsens (e.g. restricted work becomes days away).
checklist.done: columns K/L reflect current calendar-day counts consistent with HRIS absence records, capped at 180.

checklist.step: Update the log within 7 calendar days of newly learned information
actions: When new information arrives (late diagnosis, worsened outcome, case found not work-related), amend the Form 300 row within 7 calendar days — line out and correct rather than delete, per the 1904.33(b)(1) update duty that runs for the full 5-year retention period.
Remove cases determined not recordable by lining out the row and noting the basis on the recordability worksheet.
Apply the same update to stored prior-year logs when the new information concerns a prior-year case.
Note the update date and reason on the HRIS case.
checklist.done: every change to a case is reflected on the log within 7 calendar days with the reason documented.

checklist.step: Reconcile the log monthly to workers' compensation and absence data
actions: Each month, pull the workers' compensation claim feed from the carrier/TPA and the HRIS absence report filtered to occupational absence reasons.

Match every WC claim and occupational absence to a Form 300 row or a documented not-recordable worksheet; recordability is decided by Part 1904, not by claim compensability, so a denied WC claim can still be recordable.
Hand unmatched items to the establishment recordkeeper as potential missed recordables with a 7-day resolution deadline.
File the monthly reconciliation in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the month's WC claims and occupational absences all tie to a log row or a documented non-recordable call.

checklist.step: Escalate fatalities and severe events to the incident-reporting process immediately
actions: On learning of any work-related fatality, in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye, phone the People Analytics / HR Operations Manager and Employment Counsel immediately — the separate 29 CFR 1904.39 report clock (8 hours for a fatality, 24 hours for the others) is handled under REG-055-C08 and cannot wait for the log entry.
Record the event on the Form 300 within the normal 7 days regardless of the 1904.39 report.
Cross-reference the 1904.39 report confirmation number on the HRIS case.
checklist.done: severe events are handed to the C08 reporting process at once and still appear on the log within 7 days.

checklist.step: Run the year-end log review before the annual summary
actions: In January, review each establishment's Form 300 per 29 CFR 1904.32(a)(1): every entry complete and accurate, missing cases added, day counts closed or carried at the year-end value.
Verify a Form 301 exists for every 300 row and that privacy cases are masked with the concordance intact.
Confirm establishments with zero recordables will still produce a Form 300A showing zeros, as 1904.32(a)(4) requires.
Sign the review note per establishment and pass the package to the 300A certification and filing process (REG-055-C02).
checklist.done: each establishment has a signed year-end review note and a complete, accurate closing log.

checklist.step: Prove the four-business-hour production capability
actions: Twice a year, run a timed drill: a nominated requester names an establishment and year, and the recordkeeper must produce the Form 300, 300A and 301 set from the compliance evidence repository as 29 CFR 1904.40 requires within four business hours.
Log the clock start, retrieval path and elapsed time on the drill record.
Fix any establishment whose records could not be produced in time — re-index the repository folder OSHA/Recordkeeping/<establishment>/<year> and re-run the drill within 30 days.
File drill results with the annual evidence.
checklist.done: the latest drill shows every tested establishment's records produced inside four business hours.

checklist.step: Train establishment recordkeepers annually
actions: Assign the OSHA Recordkeeping course in Cornerstone LMS each January to every named recordkeeper and their backup, covering the 1904.5 work-relatedness test, the 1904.7 decision tree, first-aid list, privacy cases and the 7-day rule.
Include five scored case-study determinations drawn from the company's own prior-year cases (anonymized); require 80% to pass.
Chase non-completers at 30 days through their HR Business Partner and bar untrained staff from log-edit permissions.
Export the completion report to the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every named recordkeeper and backup holds a current-year LMS completion at 80% or better.

checklist.step: Retain the records five years and log every exception
actions: At year-end, lock the establishment workbooks and file Forms 300, 300A, 301, recordability worksheets and reconciliations in the compliance evidence repository with a retention label of 5 years following the end of the covered calendar year (29 CFR 1904.33(a)).
Raise a tracker issue for every late entry, missed recordable or coverage gap found during the year, with root cause and correcting-entry date.
Obtain Compliance Officer sign-off on each closed exception.
Verify the repository index retrieves records by establishment, year and case number.
checklist.done: the year's records carry the 5-year retention label and every exception is closed with Compliance Officer sign-off.

testing.step: Build the incident population for the test year
actions: Extract every HRIS safety-incident case with a date-of-knowledge in the test year, all fields, across all establishments.
Extract the full-year workers' compensation claim listing from the carrier/TPA feed and the HRIS occupational-absence report.
Extract each establishment's Form 300 rows from the locked workbooks.
Sign the three extracts with row counts and extraction dates into the test workpaper.
testing.done: three dated, counted extracts (incidents, WC claims, log rows) sit in the workpaper.

testing.step: Reconcile the three populations to surface missed recordables
actions: Match every WC claim and occupational absence to an HRIS incident case and every recordable-marked case to a Form 300 row, on employee + injury date + establishment.
List every WC claim with no incident case, and every recordable call with no log row, as automatic exceptions.
Confirm every establishment on the register has a current-year log — a covered establishment with no workbook is an automatic fail.
Resolve count differences before sampling.
testing.done: every claim and case is matched or listed as an exception, and every covered establishment produced a log.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of recordability decisions
actions: Take 100% of cases closed as not-recordable that had a WC claim attached — these carry the miss risk.
Take 25 randomly selected recordable cases (seeded, reproducible) spread across establishments, minimum 40 cases total.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all high-risk non-recordable calls is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the work-relatedness and recordability call on each sampled case
actions: Read the incident narrative, medical notes and WC file for the sampled case without first looking at the recorded conclusion.
Apply 29 CFR 1904.5 (including the (b)(2) exceptions and the telework rule) and the 1904.7 criteria with the first-aid list, and write an independent conclusion.
Compare to the recorded call; any difference — including right answer with wrong criterion cited — is an exception.
Note the eCFR text version relied on in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled case carries an independent re-performance note and a match/exception verdict.

testing.step: Verify 7-calendar-day entry timeliness on the sample
actions: For each sampled recordable, compute log-entry date minus date-of-knowledge from the HRIS case and the workbook version history.
Flag any gap over 7 calendar days as late; use the SharePoint file version timestamps, not the recordkeeper's asserted date, as the source of truth.
Compare the late rate to the 5% threshold.
testing.done: each sampled entry has a computed day-gap and the aggregate late rate is stated against the threshold.

testing.step: Recompute day counts and outcome columns
actions: For 10 sampled days-away or restricted cases, recompute calendar days from HRIS absence records, starting the day after injury and capping at 180.
Check exactly one outcome column (G/H/I/J) is ticked and that it reflects the most severe outcome the case reached.
Check reclassifications (e.g. restricted became days away) were made within 7 days of the change being known.
Any count off by more than one day or wrong column is an exception.
testing.done: recomputed counts and columns agree with the log or the differences are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Test privacy-case handling
actions: Screen the full-year case list for injuries meeting the 1904.29(b)(7) privacy list and confirm each shows 'Privacy Case' on the Form 300 with no employee name.
Verify the restricted concordance file resolves each privacy case number and that its access list is limited to named recordkeepers.
Treat any named privacy-qualifying case on a log as an exception requiring immediate correction.
testing.done: all privacy-qualifying cases are masked on the logs and resolvable only via the restricted concordance.

testing.step: Verify establishment coverage calls and the production drill
actions: Re-check three establishment exemption determinations against the site NAICS code and 29 CFR 1904.2 Appendix A as currently published.
Inspect the two four-business-hour drill records for the year and confirm elapsed times and any re-runs.
Pull one establishment-year at random and time an unannounced retrieval of its 300/300A/301 set from the repository.
testing.done: exemption calls re-verify, drill records exist, and the unannounced retrieval landed inside four business hours.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the case, establishment, what failed (missed recordable, late entry, wrong call, privacy breach) and the regulatory exposure.
Assign root cause (intake gap, training gap, WC feed not reconciled, telework confusion) and an owner.
Require correcting log entries within 7 calendar days of the finding and set a retest for every open item in next year's test.
Refer any pattern of suppressed reporting to Employment Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, correcting-entry date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the missed-recordable count and late-entry rate against the zero-miss / 5%-late thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Have the Internal Auditor who made none of the sampled determinations sign, with Compliance Officer countersignature.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report results to the Chief HR Officer before the 300A certification is signed.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion and thresholds is filed and reported ahead of certification.

checklist.step: Confirm which establishments must submit electronically this year
actions: Take the current covered-establishment register (from REG-055-C01) and, per establishment, pull peak employment for the prior year from the HRIS headcount report.
Apply the 29 CFR 1904.41 triggers: 250+ employees, or 20-249 employees in an industry listed in Appendix A to Subpart E — check each site's NAICS code against the appendix as published on osha.gov.
Note that every covered establishment certifies and posts a 300A even if it owes no ITA submission, and that zero recordables never excuses either duty.
Record the submit / post-only call per establishment with the NAICS and headcount basis, and have the People Analytics / HR Operations Manager countersign.
checklist.done: a countersigned worksheet states submit or post-only for every establishment with its headcount and NAICS basis.

checklist.step: Close the prior-year Form 300 logs and freeze the case data
actions: Confirm the year-end log review from REG-055-C01 is signed for each establishment before any totals are computed.
Close open day counts at the December 31 value (counting continues into the new year on the log itself, but the 300A snapshot uses the review-date values).
Lock each workbook version as 300A-source-<establishment>-<year> so later log updates cannot silently change the summary basis.
Note any case added or reclassified during review on the tie-out worksheet.
checklist.done: each establishment has a locked, review-signed log version named as the 300A source.

checklist.step: Compute the Form 300A case-count and day-count totals per establishment
actions: From the locked log, count rows into the 300A boxes: total deaths (G), cases with days away (H), cases with job transfer or restriction (I), other recordable cases (J).
Sum column K (days away) and column L (days of transfer/restriction) into the day-count totals.
Count injury/illness types M1-M6 (injuries, skin disorders, respiratory conditions, poisonings, hearing loss, all other illnesses).
Cross-foot: G+H+I+J must equal the number of log rows net of lined-out cases; investigate any difference to the row before proceeding.
Enter zeros, not blanks, for establishments with no recordables.
checklist.done: 300A totals per establishment cross-foot exactly to the locked log with zeros where applicable.

checklist.step: Compute annual average employment and total hours worked from payroll
actions: Run the payroll headcount-by-pay-period report for the establishment and compute annual average employment using the OSHA worksheet method: sum of employees paid each pay period ÷ number of pay periods, rounded to the next-highest whole number.
Run the hours report and total hours actually worked, excluding vacation, sick leave, holidays and other non-worked paid hours.
Include temporary and leased workers the company supervises day-to-day; exclude independent contractors.
Hand the two figures with the source report extracts to the Benefits Analyst and file the extracts with the tie-out worksheet.
checklist.done: each establishment has payroll-sourced average employment and hours-worked figures with extracts attached.

checklist.step: Assemble and quality-check the 300A per establishment
actions: Complete the Form 300A header: establishment name, street address, industry description, NAICS code, annual average employment and total hours worked.
Paste the case, day and illness-type totals from the tie-out worksheet.
Have a second Benefits Analyst re-add every box independently and initial the worksheet.
Save the completed 300A as a PDF per establishment in the SharePoint summary folder.
checklist.done: a second-checked 300A PDF exists per establishment with a complete header.

checklist.step: Obtain company-executive certification of each 300A
actions: Route each 300A to a qualifying certifier under 29 CFR 1904.32(b)(4): an owner, officer of the corporation, the highest-ranking company official working at the establishment, or that official's immediate supervisor.

The certifier examines the underlying Form 300, questions the preparer on anything unclear, and signs and dates the 300A attesting they reasonably believe it is complete and accurate — 1904.32(b)(3) makes this a knowledge-based attestation, not a rubber stamp.
Reject for rework any 300A whose totals the certifier cannot tie to the log in front of them.
Record certifier name, title and date on the certification register.
checklist.done: every 300A carries a qualifying executive's dated signature recorded on the certification register.

checklist.step: Post the certified 300A at every establishment by February 1
actions: Send each site's certified 300A to its office manager by January 25 with posting instructions: post in the conspicuous place where employee notices are customarily posted, no later than February 1, and keep it up through April 30 per 29 CFR 1904.32(b)(5)-(6).
Require a dated photo of the posted summary in place from each site, returned by February 1.
For establishments with no fixed worksite or remote-only staff, distribute the 300A by email/intranet and record the distribution list and date.
Chase any site without a photo on February 1 the same day and log the delay as an exception.
Diarize April 30 and instruct sites not to remove the posting before then.
checklist.done: a dated posting photo or distribution record exists for every establishment showing the 300A up by February 1.

checklist.step: Prepare the ITA account and establishment records
actions: Log in to the OSHA Injury Tracking Application at ita.osha.gov using the company Login.gov credentials; verify the account holder is current staff and update the contact email if not.
Under Establishment List, confirm every must-submit establishment exists with the correct name, address, NAICS code and EIN; add or edit establishments where the register changed.
Mark ceased or divested locations appropriately rather than deleting history.
Screenshot the reconciled establishment list into the evidence folder.
checklist.done: the ITA establishment list matches the must-submit worksheet exactly, evidenced by a dated screenshot.

checklist.step: Submit the 300A data through the ITA by March 2
actions: In the ITA choose manual entry per establishment or the batch CSV upload built from the certified 300A PDFs — never from the live logs, which may have moved on.
Enter for each establishment: average employment, total hours worked, and the case, day and illness-type totals, exactly as certified.

Where the company is required under 1904.41(a)(2) to also submit Form 300/301 case data (100+ employees in a high-hazard designated industry), complete the case-detail upload with privacy-case names withheld.
Submit no later than March 2, resolve any ITA validation errors the same day, and download the submission confirmation receipt per establishment.
File receipts in the compliance evidence repository and mark the compliance calendar item complete.
checklist.done: every must-submit establishment shows a completed ITA submission dated on or before March 2 with receipts filed.

checklist.step: Handle state-plan submission differences
actions: For establishments in State Plan states, check the state agency's recordkeeping page for adopted electronic-submission rules and any state-specific portal or extra fields.
Where the State Plan directs submission through the federal ITA (the common case), record that determination; where it differs, diary the state deadline and channel on the compliance calendar.
Save the state-page capture with date into the evidence folder for each such establishment.
checklist.done: every State-Plan establishment has a dated determination of channel and deadline with source capture.

checklist.step: Verify posting stayed up through April 30 and take-down
actions: In mid-March and mid-April, spot-request fresh dated photos from a rotating third of sites to confirm the 300A is still posted.
On May 1, notify sites they may remove the summary; retain the posted copy in the site file.
Log any site found without the posting during the window as an exception with re-posting the same day.
checklist.done: spot-check photos cover the posting window and the take-down notice went out May 1.

checklist.step: Process corrections and resubmissions
actions: When a log correction (from the 1904.33(b) update duty) changes a certified total, recompute the 300A, obtain re-certification, and re-post if within the Feb 1-Apr 30 window.
Re-open the establishment's ITA submission, edit the affected figures, and resubmit; download the new receipt.
Record the correction chain — log change, re-certification date, ITA resubmission date — on the tie-out worksheet.
checklist.done: every post-certification correction shows a complete re-certify / re-post / resubmit chain with receipts.

checklist.step: Log deadline exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any establishment that posted after February 1, removed the posting early, or submitted to the ITA after March 2, recording the days late.
Assign root cause (payroll data late, certifier unavailable, ITA credential lockout, register gap) and an owner.

Note that a submission failure sits exposed to OSHA's other-than-serious citation authority and to the ITA non-filer enforcement lists, and brief Employment Counsel on any item more than 30 days late.
Close each issue only with Compliance Officer sign-off.
checklist.done: every deadline miss is tracked with days late, root cause, owner and signed disposition.

checklist.step: Retain the annual-cycle evidence set
actions: File per establishment: locked log source, tie-out worksheet, payroll extracts, certified 300A, posting photos, ITA receipts and any correction chain, under OSHA/AnnualSummary/<year>/<establishment>.
Apply the 5-year retention label per 29 CFR 1904.33(a).
Test-retrieve one establishment's full set to confirm the four-business-hour capability extends to summary records.
checklist.done: the complete evidence set is filed, labelled 5 years, and test-retrieved successfully.

checklist.step: Run the post-cycle debrief and update the procedure
actions: In April, review the cycle: dates achieved versus the Feb 1 / Mar 2 deadlines, exceptions raised, and ITA validation issues encountered.
Update the Annual Summary Procedure for any ITA collection changes, register changes or new State-Plan rules.
Present the cycle result and open exceptions to the Chief HR Officer and Compliance Officer.
Set next year's compliance calendar entries before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: a debrief note is filed, the procedure is updated, and next year's calendar entries exist.

testing.step: Build the establishment population and the cycle record set
actions: Pull the covered-establishment register and the must-submit worksheet for the tested year.
Collect per establishment: locked log source, tie-out worksheet, certified 300A, posting evidence, ITA receipt.
Confirm the record set is complete for 100% of establishments — a missing certified 300A or receipt is an immediate exception.
Record counts and gaps in the test workpaper.
testing.done: a complete-or-excepted record set exists for every establishment on the register.

testing.step: Reconcile the must-submit determinations
actions: Independently re-apply the 29 CFR 1904.41 triggers to each establishment using HRIS peak-employment data and the current Appendix A industry list.
Compare to the recorded submit / post-only calls; any establishment wrongly classed post-only is a high-severity exception.
Verify no covered establishment was omitted from the register itself by tying the register to the HRIS location list.
testing.done: every submit/post-only call re-verifies against headcount and NAICS, and the register ties to the HRIS.

testing.step: Recompute 300A totals from the locked logs for a sample
actions: Select all establishments with 10+ recordables plus a random 5 others (seeded, reproducible); minimum 8 establishments.
Recount G/H/I/J cases, K/L day totals and M1-M6 types directly from the locked log version.
Compare to the certified 300A; any difference of any size is an exception per the zero-tolerance threshold.
Record the recount sheets in the workpaper.
testing.done: recounted totals match the certified 300A exactly for every sampled establishment, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Recompute average employment and hours worked
actions: For the sampled establishments, rerun the payroll pay-period headcount and hours reports for the tested year.
Recompute average employment by the OSHA worksheet method and total worked hours excluding paid non-worked time.
Compare to the certified figures; flag any variance over 5% and trace it to the source report.
testing.done: recomputed employment and hours are within 5% of certified figures or the variance is logged with cause.

testing.step: Verify certification qualification and dates
actions: For each sampled 300A, check the certifier against the 29 CFR 1904.32(b)(4) list using the HRIS org chart as of the signing date.
Confirm the signature date is on or before February 1 and precedes the posting evidence date.
Treat a certification by an unqualified signer as a fail requiring re-certification.
testing.done: every sampled certification is by a qualifying official, dated on or before February 1.

testing.step: Verify posting evidence across the Feb 1 - Apr 30 window
actions: Inspect the February 1 posting photos and metadata dates for the sampled establishments.
Inspect the mid-window spot-check evidence and the May 1 take-down notice.
For remote-distribution establishments, verify the distribution list covers all assigned employees per the HRIS.
Log any window gap with its day count.
testing.done: posting evidence covers Feb 1 through Apr 30 for each sampled establishment or gaps are quantified.

testing.step: Trace ITA submissions to receipts and re-verify timeliness
actions: Log in to the ITA (view access) and compare each must-submit establishment's submission status and timestamp to the filed receipt.
Confirm every submission timestamp is on or before March 2 and the submitted figures equal the certified 300A.
Verify any correction was resubmitted and the final ITA figures match the final certified totals.
Screenshot the ITA status list into the workpaper.
testing.done: every must-submit establishment shows an on-time ITA submission whose figures match certification.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths on exceptions
actions: For every logged exception, recompute days late from the evidence timestamps rather than the issue narrative.
Check the exception was raised contemporaneously, not during audit fieldwork.
Confirm counsel was briefed on any item over 30 days late as the procedure requires.
testing.done: exception day-counts re-verify from source timestamps and escalation rules were followed.

testing.step: Log test exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per test exception with establishment, failure type and regulatory exposure.
Assign root cause (tie-out skipped, payroll method wrong, unqualified certifier, ITA credential gap) and an owner with a remediation date.
Set mandatory retest of every open item in the next annual cycle test.
testing.done: each test exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest flag.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the cycle test
actions: State the results against the thresholds: 100% on-time certification/posting/submission, exact tie-outs, 5% payroll variance.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Obtain sign-off from an Internal Auditor independent of the cycle and countersignature from the Compliance Officer.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report to the Chief HR Officer and the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed, filed workpaper states the conclusion and was reported to the CHRO and committee.

checklist.step: Maintain the OSHA poster at every establishment
actions: Download the current OSHA 3165 'Job Safety and Health: It's the Law' poster from osha.gov/publications/poster and check the edition against the placement register.
For State Plan states, obtain the state's equivalent poster from the state agency site and note which poster each establishment requires.
Instruct each site office manager to display the poster where employee notices are customarily posted and return a dated photo.
Update the placement register (establishment, poster edition, language versions displayed, photo date) and re-verify semi-annually.
Publish the poster on the HR intranet for remote employees and record the page location.
checklist.done: the placement register shows a current-edition poster photo for every establishment and an intranet posting for remote staff.

checklist.step: Publish and maintain the injury-reporting procedure notice
actions: Draft the notice required by 29 CFR 1904.35(b)(1)(i)-(iii): how to report a work-related injury or illness, that reporting is prompt-and-accurate but the procedure must be reasonable and not deter reporting, and that retaliation is prohibited.
Have Employment Counsel review the wording against the 1904.35(b)(1)(iv) anti-retaliation standard before publication.
Publish on the HR intranet and place the notice in the new-hire onboarding pack in the HRIS onboarding task list.
Re-issue to all staff by email whenever the reporting channel changes, and log the send.
checklist.done: a counsel-reviewed reporting-procedure notice is live on the intranet, in onboarding, and re-issued on every channel change.

checklist.step: Verify every new hire receives the reporting notice
actions: Configure the HRIS onboarding checklist so the injury-reporting notice task must be acknowledged within the first week.
Run the monthly onboarding-completion report and chase any hire past 14 days without acknowledgment through their manager.
Export the monthly acknowledgment report to the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: monthly reports show every new hire acknowledged the notice within 14 days or is under active chase.

checklist.step: Intake record requests through a single queue with the right SLA
actions: Open a ticket for every request for OSHA records, capturing requester name, requester type (current employee, former employee, personal representative, authorized employee representative, government representative), records sought and establishment/year.

Set the SLA from the deadline table: Form 300 copy — end of the next business day; Form 301 to the injured employee — within 7 calendar days; Form 301 'Tell us about the case' section to an authorized representative — within 7 calendar days; government representative — four business hours.
Timestamp the intake from the first contact (email arrival, call log), not the ticket creation time.
Route government-representative tickets simultaneously to Employment Counsel.
checklist.done: every request has a ticket with requester type, correct SLA and a first-contact timestamp.

checklist.step: Verify requester identity and entitlement before release
actions: For employees and former employees, confirm identity against the HRIS record and their employment at the establishment/year requested.
For a personal representative, obtain the written designation or legal authority document and attach it to the ticket.
For an authorized employee representative (e.g. a union agent under a collective bargaining agreement), verify the representation against the agreement and record the basis.
For government representatives, verify credentials (OSHA CSHO card, HHS/NIOSH or state-plan identification) and record the officer's name, office and phone on the ticket.
checklist.done: each ticket shows the entitlement basis with supporting document or credential noted before anything was released.

checklist.step: Prepare Form 300 copies with the correct privacy handling
actions: Copy the requested establishment-year Form 300 from the compliance evidence repository — never hand over the working file.
Leave 'Privacy Case' masking in place; per 29 CFR 1904.35(b)(2)(iv) the employee-access copy keeps names except privacy cases, which remain masked for everyone except the government.
For an authorized employee representative, additionally remove or verify masking of privacy-case identifiers per 1904.35(b)(2)(v)(B).
Record on the ticket exactly which pages and years were released.
checklist.done: the released 300 copy carries correct privacy masking and the ticket lists the exact contents.

checklist.step: Prepare Form 301 releases by requester type
actions: To the injured/ill employee or their personal representative: release the full Form 301 for their own case within 7 calendar days.

To an authorized employee representative: release only the 'Tell us about the case' section (fields 10-18), redacting the left-hand employee and physician information fields, within 7 calendar days per 1904.35(b)(2)(v)(B).
Have a second HR Specialist verify the redaction before release and initial the ticket.
Attach the released version to the ticket.
checklist.done: each 301 release matches the requester's entitlement, is second-checked, and is attached to the ticket.

checklist.step: Fulfil employee requests inside the statutory clocks
actions: Deliver Form 300 copies by the end of the business day after the request; deliver 301 releases within 7 calendar days.
Deliver free of charge for the first copy per 1904.35(b)(2)(iii)-(iv), by the requester's preferred channel (secure email or collection).
Close the ticket with the delivery timestamp and delivery proof (send record or signed receipt).
If the deadline is at risk, escalate to the HR Operations Manager before it passes, not after.
checklist.done: the ticket shows delivery proof timestamped inside the next-business-day or 7-calendar-day clock.

checklist.step: Run the four-business-hour government production
actions: On a verified request from an authorized government representative (OSHA, HHS/NIOSH, or a state-plan agency), start the clock at the request time per 29 CFR 1904.40(a) and note business hours run 8:00-17:00 local time at the establishment.
Pull the requested 300/300A/301 records from the compliance evidence repository using the indexed establishment-year path proven by the C01 retrieval drills.
Have Employment Counsel scan the set — production to the government includes privacy-case names per 1904.40, so do not over-redact, but nothing beyond the request goes in the set.
Hand over the copies, record clock start, hand-over time and contents on the ticket, and confirm elapsed time was within four business hours.
checklist.done: the ticket evidences production of the exact requested set inside four business hours with counsel review noted.

checklist.step: Log and cure any missed deadline immediately
actions: On any SLA breach, complete the delivery first, then raise a tracker issue with elapsed time versus the clock and the requester type.
For a government-production miss, notify Employment Counsel the same day to assess exposure and any proactive communication to the requesting office.
Assign root cause (index failure, absent recordkeeper, credential verification delay) and a fix with an owner and date.
checklist.done: every breach shows completed delivery, a tracker issue with elapsed time, and counsel notice where governmental.

checklist.step: Keep notice content current with rule and poster changes
actions: Watch the Federal Register and OSHA QuickTakes for Part 1904 or poster-edition changes; check state-plan sites for the establishments' states quarterly.
On a change, update the deadline table, poster register requirement and notice text within 30 days, with Employment Counsel review.
Record the watch log entries and each change's implementation date.
checklist.done: the quarterly watch log is current and every rule/poster change shows an implementation inside 30 days.

checklist.step: Brief site office managers annually
actions: Assign the annual notices-and-access briefing in the LMS to every site office manager: poster duty, what to do when an OSHA officer appears (call HR Coordinator and Employment Counsel at once — the four-hour clock is running), and never to release records directly.
Include the walk-in scenario as a scored question.
Export completions to the compliance evidence repository and chase non-completers at 30 days.
checklist.done: every site office manager holds a current-year briefing completion.

checklist.step: Reconcile the request log quarterly
actions: Each quarter, export closed tickets and reconcile against the HR shared-mailbox search for records-request keywords to catch requests that bypassed the queue.
Open a late ticket for any bypassed request found, fulfil it, and log it as an exception.
Report the quarter's volumes, SLA performance and exceptions to the HR Operations Manager.
checklist.done: the quarterly reconciliation found-and-fixed any bypassed requests and the SLA report is issued.

checklist.step: Retain notice and access evidence
actions: File the poster register, notice distribution logs, acknowledgment reports and closed tickets with release copies under OSHA/NoticesAccess/<year>.
Apply the 5-year retention label aligned to the underlying records year.
Verify retrieval by requester name and by establishment-year.
checklist.done: the year's notice and access evidence is filed, labelled and retrievable.

checklist.step: Review anti-retaliation signals from the request channel
actions: Review quarterly whether any employee who requested records or reported an injury subsequently faced discipline, and cross-check against the employee-relations case log.
Refer any temporal pattern to Employment Counsel for a Section 11(c) / 1904.35(b)(1)(iv) risk assessment (handled substantively under REG-055-C04).
Document the quarterly review even when clean.
checklist.done: a documented quarterly review exists with referrals made where patterns appeared.

testing.step: Build the ticket population and reconcile it to intake channels
actions: Export all record-request tickets closed in the test year with requester type, timestamps and attachments.
Independently search the HR shared mailbox and call logs for request keywords in two sample months and match hits to tickets.
List any request with no ticket as an exception — the population must be complete before SLAs mean anything.
Record counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: the ticket population reconciles to independent channel searches with unmatched requests excepted.

testing.step: Draw the sample across requester types
actions: Take 100% of government-representative tickets and 100% of tickets involving privacy cases.
Add 20 randomly selected employee/representative tickets (seeded, reproducible); minimum 30 total.
Record seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all government and privacy tickets plus a random employee slice.

testing.step: Recompute every sampled SLA from source timestamps
actions: Take the first-contact timestamp from the original email or call record, not the ticket field, and the delivery timestamp from the send record or receipt.
Recompute against the correct clock: next business day for 300 copies, 7 calendar days for 301 releases, four business hours (8:00-17:00 local) for government productions.
Flag any ticket where the intake timestamp was set later than first contact — clock manipulation is a severity-one finding.
testing.done: every sampled ticket has a recomputed elapsed time against the correct statutory clock.

testing.step: Inspect released documents for entitlement and redaction
actions: Open each sampled ticket's attached release copy and compare contents to the requester's entitlement (full 301 vs 'Tell us about the case' section only; privacy masking on 300 copies).
Verify the entitlement document (representative designation, credential note) is attached.
Any unredacted privacy identifier released to a non-government requester is an automatic fail referred to Employment Counsel.
testing.done: every sampled release matches entitlement with correct redaction, or failures are referred to counsel.

testing.step: Re-perform a government-production drill unannounced
actions: Acting as the drill requester, name a random establishment and year and start a logged clock.
Observe the HR Coordinator retrieve, counsel-review and assemble the production set without assisting.
Stop the clock at hand-over and compare elapsed time to four business hours.
File the drill log in the workpaper.
testing.done: the unannounced drill produced the correct set inside four business hours with the log filed.

testing.step: Verify poster coverage independently
actions: Select 5 establishments (seeded) and request same-day dated photos directly from site office managers, bypassing the HR Coordinator.
Compare the photographed poster edition and state variant against the placement register and the current osha.gov/state edition.
Check the intranet poster page is live and linked from the reporting-procedure notice.
testing.done: independent photos confirm current posters at all sampled sites and the intranet posting is live.

testing.step: Test new-hire notice coverage
actions: Pull the year's new-hire cohort from the HRIS and match each hire to a reporting-notice acknowledgment.
Compute the acknowledgment rate and the median days-to-acknowledge.
List hires with no acknowledgment beyond 14 days who were never chased as exceptions.
testing.done: the cohort acknowledgment rate is computed and unchased gaps are excepted.

testing.step: Verify breach handling followed the procedure
actions: For every SLA breach in the year, confirm a contemporaneous tracker issue exists with elapsed time and root cause.
Confirm Employment Counsel was notified same-day on governmental misses.
Check remediations (index fixes, backup recordkeepers) were actually implemented by re-inspecting the fix.
testing.done: every breach shows a contemporaneous issue, required counsel notice, and an implemented fix.

testing.step: Log test exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise an issue per exception with ticket reference, failure type and exposure.
Assign root cause (queue bypass, redaction miss, clock manipulation, poster gap) with owner and remediation date.
Flag clock-manipulation and privacy-release findings for Employment Counsel and the CHRO regardless of count.
Set retest of open items in next year's test.
testing.done: all exceptions are tracked with owner, date, counsel referrals and retest flags.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute results against the thresholds: ≥95% employee SLA, zero privacy mis-releases, 100% posters, 100% government productions in four hours.
Write the conclusion with workpaper references.
Obtain independent reviewer sign-off (an Internal Auditor who fulfilled no sampled request) and Compliance Officer countersignature.
File in the compliance evidence repository and report to the CHRO.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion against all four thresholds is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Open the annual review and fix the analysis window
actions: On February 1, open the annual review task with the prior calendar year as the analysis window and March 31 as the completion date.
Re-read 29 CFR 1904.35(b)(1) and the October 11 2018 OSHA memorandum on drug testing and incentive programs; note any new interpretation letters counsel has flagged since last year.
Confirm the review team: Employee Relations Manager (lead), People Analytics / HR Operations Manager (data), Employment Counsel (privilege and judgement calls).
Record the scope note in the workpaper.
checklist.done: the review is open with window, team, completion date and a current-law scope note.

checklist.step: Pull the injury-reporter cohort and the discipline data
actions: Extract every employee who reported a work-related injury or illness in the window plus the preceding 12 months, from the HRIS safety-incident cases.
Extract all discipline actions (warnings, suspensions, demotions, terminations, hour reductions) and performance-improvement plans for the same period with action dates and stated reasons.
Join the two sets on employee id and compute days between injury report and each subsequent adverse action.
Deliver the joined extract to the Employee Relations Manager with row counts.
checklist.done: a joined extract of reporters and adverse actions with day-gaps exists with recorded counts.

checklist.step: Run the 90-day proximity screen
actions: Flag every adverse action within 90 days after an injury report for individual file review.

For each flagged case, pull the ER case file and the disciplinary documentation and write down the stated business reason, the rule applied, and whether non-reporting employees were treated the same for the same conduct.
Classify each case: clean (documented reason, consistent treatment), review (documentation thin), or refer (temporal link plus inconsistent treatment).
Send every 'refer' case to Employment Counsel the same week.
checklist.done: every 90-day-proximate action is classified with a written rationale and referrals sent.

checklist.step: Review disciplinary rules that punish reporting mechanics
actions: Read the attendance, late-reporting and 'immediate reporting' rules in the employee handbook against 1904.35(b)(1)(i): a procedure requiring reporting 'as soon as practicable after realizing' an injury is reasonable; discipline for reporting 'late' when symptoms emerged gradually is deterrence.
List every discipline action in the window issued for how or when an injury was reported (as opposed to the underlying safety conduct).
Mark rules or actions that punish the report itself for redesign or rescission.
Draft the required wording fix with Employment Counsel.
checklist.done: reporting-mechanics rules are assessed with each deterrent rule marked and a counsel-drafted fix in hand.

checklist.step: Audit post-incident drug-testing decisions
actions: List every post-incident drug test in the window from the ER log and the occupational-health vendor invoices.

For each, check a documented reasonable basis existed that drug use likely contributed to the incident and that the test could measure impairment (per the 2018 memorandum, blanket automatic testing after every reported injury is a deterrence indicator; tests under state workers' comp premium-reduction statutes or DOT rules are permissible).
Record the basis or its absence per test.
Refer every basis-free test to Employment Counsel and propose the policy correction if a blanket rule caused it.
checklist.done: every post-incident test shows a documented permissible basis or is referred with a policy correction proposed.

checklist.step: Assess safety incentive programs against the memorandum
actions: Inventory every active safety incentive: site bonuses tied to recordable counts, prize draws for injury-free periods, manager scorecards containing injury rates.

Test each against the 2018 memorandum: rate-based programs that withhold a benefit because someone reported are deterrent unless adequate precautions exist (parallel leading-indicator incentives, anti-retaliation training, procedures making clear reporting is never penalized).
Redesign or add precautions to any failing program — e.g. shift the metric to near-miss reporting, training completion or hazard closures.
Document each program's verdict and change in the workpaper.
checklist.done: every incentive program has a documented verdict and any deterrent design is redesigned or buttressed.

checklist.step: Compare establishment reporting rates for suppression signals
actions: Compute each establishment's recordable rate per 200,000 hours worked (TRIR) from the C01 logs and payroll hours.
Flag any establishment below 40% of the company mean or reporting zero with 50+ employees — improbably low is a suppression signal, not a trophy.
For flagged sites, interview a sample of employees and the site manager about reporting comfort, and review first-aid logs and WC claims for unreported candidates.
Write a finding per flagged site: clean, training needed, or suppression suspected (refer to counsel).
checklist.done: per-establishment rates are computed and every low outlier has an investigated finding.

checklist.step: Handle complaint-triggered reviews inside 10 business days
actions: When an ER case is tagged 'retaliation — safety reporting', open the review task the same day and preserve the employee's file, the manager's communications and relevant system logs immediately.
Interview the reporter, the deciding manager and witnesses within the 10-business-day SLA.
Deliver a written finding to Employment Counsel with a remedy recommendation (rescind, restore pay, retrain) — remembering the employee's own 30-day window to file with OSHA runs regardless.
Track the remedy to completion in the case tool.
checklist.done: each tagged case shows same-day preservation, interviews inside 10 business days and a counsel-reviewed finding.

checklist.step: Deliver remedies and rescissions
actions: For every sustained finding, execute the remedy in the HRIS: rescind the disciplinary record, restore pay or hours with Payroll, and correct the performance file.
Notify the employee in writing of the correction.
Deliver coaching or discipline to the retaliating manager proportionate to the finding.
Evidence each step on the tracker issue.
checklist.done: sustained findings show executed HRIS corrections, employee notice, and manager consequence, all evidenced.

checklist.step: Refresh manager anti-retaliation training
actions: Assign the annual anti-retaliation module to every people manager: what 1904.35(b)(1)(iv) and Section 11(c) prohibit, the 90-day proximity risk, drug-testing limits, and how to raise performance issues without touching the report.
Rebuild scenarios each year from the (anonymized) findings of the last review.
Require 100% completion by June 30; chase through HR Business Partners at 30 days.
File the completion export.
checklist.done: all people managers complete the current-year module by June 30 with the export filed.

checklist.step: Update the reporting-procedure notice from review findings
actions: Feed rule changes (reporting-mechanics fixes, drug-test policy corrections, incentive redesigns) into the reporting-procedure notice maintained under REG-055-C03.
Have Employment Counsel approve the revised text.
Confirm republication on the intranet and in onboarding within 30 days of the review closing.
checklist.done: review-driven policy changes are live in the published notice within 30 days, counsel-approved.

checklist.step: Report the annual review to governance
actions: Write the annual report: cohort sizes, proximity-screen results, drug-test and incentive verdicts, establishment-rate outliers, remedies delivered, open Section 11(c) matters.
Present to the Chief HR Officer and the Compliance Officer by March 31.
Log agreed actions with owners and dates in the tracker.
checklist.done: the annual report is presented by March 31 with actions tracked.

checklist.step: Maintain the Section 11(c) complaint response readiness
actions: Keep a response playbook current: OSHA Whistleblower Protection Program contact handling, 20-day position-statement expectations, evidence assembly from the review workpapers.
On any complaint notice, issue a litigation hold over the employee's records the same day.
Run a tabletop of the playbook annually with the Employee Relations Manager.
checklist.done: the playbook is current, holds issue same-day on notices, and the annual tabletop is logged.

checklist.step: Log review findings as tracked exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue per sustained finding and per deterrent rule/program with the remedy, owner and due date.
Verify counsel sign-off is attached before closure.
Carry unremediated items into next year's review scope automatically.
checklist.done: every finding is a tracked issue closed only with counsel sign-off, with carryover armed.

checklist.step: Retain the review evidence
actions: File the workpaper, extracts, per-case rationales, program assessments and remedy evidence under OSHA/AntiRetaliation/<year> with a 5-year retention label.
Mark counsel-directed materials privileged and restrict access accordingly.
Verify retrieval by employee id and by establishment.
checklist.done: the review file is retained 5 years with privilege markings and verified retrieval.

testing.step: Rebuild the reporter-discipline population independently
actions: Re-extract injury reporters and adverse actions for the review window directly from the HRIS, without using the review team's files.
Reconcile row counts to the review's extract; any case present in the audit pull but absent from the review is an exception.
Reconcile post-incident drug tests to occupational-health vendor invoices to prove that population was complete.
testing.done: the independent pull reconciles to the review population with gaps excepted.

testing.step: Re-run the proximity computation
actions: Recompute report-to-action day gaps for the full joined population.
Compare the set of ≤90-day cases to the review's flagged list; a case the review failed to flag is an exception regardless of its merits.
Verify the window covered the preceding-12-month reporters, not just same-year reporters.
testing.done: the recomputed flag list matches the review's or misses are excepted.

testing.step: Sample and re-judge individual case classifications
actions: Take 100% of 'refer' cases and 10 seeded-random 'clean' cases.
Read each disciplinary file blind and form an independent classification against the legitimate-business-reason and consistent-treatment tests.
Any 'clean' the auditor would have referred is an exception; route disagreement to Employment Counsel for a ruling.
Document each re-judgement note.
testing.done: sampled classifications are independently re-judged with disagreements ruled by counsel.

testing.step: Verify drug-test verdicts against the memorandum
actions: For each sampled post-incident test, read the documented basis and check it states an impairment-contribution rationale or a statutory carve-out (state WC statute, DOT rule).
Confirm no blanket automatic-test policy remained in force at year-end by reading the current policy text.
Trace each referred basis-free test to its policy correction.
testing.done: sampled tests show valid bases, no blanket policy survives, and corrections trace through.

testing.step: Re-perform one incentive-program assessment
actions: Pick the largest active incentive program by spend and independently assess its design against the 2018 memorandum's deterrence test and required precautions.
Compare to the review's verdict; verify any mandated redesign is actually live in the plan documents and payout rules.
Interview two participating managers on how a mid-period injury report affects the payout in practice.
testing.done: the re-assessed program matches the review verdict and redesigns are live in payout rules.

testing.step: Recompute establishment rates and outlier handling
actions: Recompute TRIR per establishment from the locked C01 logs and payroll hours.
Re-derive the below-40%-of-mean outlier list and compare to the review's list.
For one investigated outlier, verify the interviews and first-aid-log checks documented actually occurred (calendar entries, notes).
testing.done: the outlier list re-derives identically and investigation evidence is corroborated.

testing.step: Test complaint-triggered review timeliness
actions: Pull all cases tagged 'retaliation — safety reporting' and recompute preservation-date and interview-completion SLAs from system timestamps.
Verify litigation holds issued same-day where counsel was engaged.
Flag any case where the 10-business-day SLA was recorded met but interview calendar entries say otherwise.
testing.done: all tagged cases show recomputed SLAs met from source timestamps or are excepted.

testing.step: Trace remedies into the HRIS and payroll
actions: For every sustained finding, inspect the HRIS record to confirm the discipline was actually rescinded and the performance file corrected.
Trace restored pay to the payroll register for the correct period and amount.
Confirm the written employee notice exists on file.
testing.done: every sustained remedy is verified in the HRIS, payroll register and correspondence file.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise an issue per exception (missed flag, wrong classification, unexecuted remedy, stale policy) with root cause and owner.
Refer any indication of actual retaliation left unremedied to Employment Counsel and the CHRO immediately.
Set remediation dates and next-cycle retest flags.
testing.done: all exceptions are tracked, escalations made, and retests armed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the verification
actions: State results against the thresholds: zero unremedied tainted actions, zero blanket testing policies, outlier investigations complete.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Sign as independent reviewer (no involvement in reviewed decisions) with Compliance Officer countersignature.
File the workpaper and report to the CHRO and Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed conclusion against all thresholds is filed and reported to governance.

checklist.step: Tie the plan inventory to the establishment register
actions: Pull the establishment register (from REG-055-C01) and the plan inventory from the GRC business-continuity module.

Confirm every establishment has an Emergency Action Plan and Fire Prevention Plan record; per 1910.38(b) and 1910.39(b) sites with 10 or fewer employees may communicate the plan orally — record which sites use the oral option and the basis headcount.
Open a plan-creation task for any site with neither a written plan nor a documented oral-plan determination.
Save the tie-out with date to the evidence folder.
checklist.done: every establishment maps to a written plan or a documented oral-plan determination with headcount basis.

checklist.step: Verify each EAP contains the six 1910.38(c) minimum elements
actions: Check each plan against the element checklist: (1) procedures for reporting a fire or other emergency; (2) emergency evacuation procedures and route assignments including exit maps; (3) procedures for employees who remain to operate critical operations before evacuating; (4) procedures to account for all employees after evacuation, naming the assembly point and the counting method; (5) rescue and medical duties for designated employees; (6) name or job title of every employee who may be contacted for plan information.
Mark each element present/absent on the checklist row for the plan.
Open a remediation task for any absent element with a 30-day due date.
Confirm the alarm system requirement (1910.38(d), per 1910.165) is addressed for the site.
checklist.done: each plan has a completed six-element checklist with remediation tasks for any gap.

checklist.step: Verify Fire Prevention Plan content per 1910.39(c)
actions: Check each FPP lists the major fire hazards (server/comms rooms, mailroom equipment, kitchen appliances, paper storage), their handling and storage procedures, ignition-source controls, and the housekeeping procedures for combustible waste.
Confirm the plan names the employees or job titles responsible for maintaining heat-producing equipment and for fuel-source hazard control.
Cross-check extinguisher placements against the facilities maintenance contract and the 1910.157(e) annual maintenance check record where extinguishers are provided for employee use.
checklist.done: each FPP covers hazards, controls, named maintainers, and extinguisher maintenance evidence is on file.

checklist.step: Run the annual PPE hazard assessment for exposed roles
actions: For roles with physical exposure — mailroom staff, facilities technicians, field claims adjusters entering damaged properties — walk the tasks and assess hazards per 29 CFR 1910.132(d): impact, penetration, compression, chemical, heat, dust and falling-object exposures.
Specify the PPE per hazard (safety glasses, gloves, hard hats and high-visibility vests for catastrophe field work) and record it on the assessment form.
Sign the written certification identifying the workplace evaluated, the certifier, the assessment dates and the document as the required certification per 1910.132(d)(2).
Hand the PPE list to Procurement and the affected managers, and confirm issue records for each exposed employee.
checklist.done: a signed hazard-assessment certification exists per exposed role family with PPE issue records.

checklist.step: Complete the annual plan review by June 30
actions: Work the GRC review task per establishment: re-read the plan on-site or with the site office manager, walk the evacuation routes, and verify exits, maps and assembly points match the current floor layout.
Update the plan for any layout, tenancy or alarm-system change found.
Record the review completion in the GRC task with reviewer, date and changes made.
Chase any establishment approaching June 30 unreviewed at the 7-day alert.
checklist.done: every establishment's GRC review task is completed by June 30 with documented changes.

checklist.step: Maintain the floor-warden and critical-operations rosters
actions: Quarterly, reconcile the warden roster per floor against the HRIS active-employee list for that establishment.
Replace departed or relocated wardens within 15 days and record the appointment acceptance.
Verify each named critical-operations employee (e.g. data-center shutdown steps) still holds the role and knows the delay-then-evacuate procedure.
Publish the updated roster to the site intranet page and the assembly-point placard.
checklist.done: the quarterly reconciliation shows no departed wardens and rosters are republished.

checklist.step: Train employees on the plan at the 1910.38(e)-(f) trigger points
actions: Assign EAP training in the LMS at the three required points: initial assignment (new hire or site transfer), when the employee's plan responsibilities change, and when the plan itself changes.
Cover the reporting procedure, their evacuation route, assembly point and accounting method.
Trigger the plan-change retraining automatically from the GRC plan-version update event.
Export completions monthly and chase gaps past 14 days.
checklist.done: training records show coverage at all three trigger points with no gap older than 14 days unchased.

checklist.step: Update plans within 30 days of moves and reconfigurations
actions: Subscribe the plan-update task to facilities move/reconfiguration tickets in ServiceNow so each ticket auto-opens a plan task with a 30-day SLA.
Update evacuation maps, route assignments and assembly points for the new layout; reprint and re-post floor maps.
Trigger the plan-change retraining for affected employees.
Close the task with the new plan version id linked to the move ticket.
checklist.done: every move ticket links to a closed plan-update task inside 30 days with retraining triggered.

checklist.step: Keep the plan available to employees for review
actions: Post the current EAP and evacuation maps on each site's intranet page and keep a printed copy at reception, satisfying the 1910.38(b) availability requirement.
Verify availability during the annual review walk and after every version change.
For oral-plan small sites, document who communicates the plan and when each employee last received it.
checklist.done: current plans are posted and available at every site, with oral-plan communication logged for small sites.

checklist.step: Integrate the people-safety chapter into the continuity plan set
actions: Align the business-continuity plan's life-safety chapter (evacuation, accounting, emergency communications cascade) with the establishment EAPs so the two never give conflicting instructions.
Reference the mass-notification tool's emergency templates and confirm the employee contact data refresh from the HRIS is running monthly.
Record the alignment check as part of the annual review.
checklist.done: the BC life-safety chapter matches the EAPs and the contact-data refresh is evidenced monthly.

checklist.step: Capture post-incident and post-drill lessons into the plans
actions: After every real evacuation, alarm activation or drill (drills run under REG-055-C06), collect the accounting time, blocked-route and missing-person findings.
Amend the affected plan within 30 days and re-issue with a new version id.
Trigger retraining where routes or assembly points changed.
checklist.done: every incident/drill finding traces to a plan amendment within 30 days or a documented no-change rationale.

checklist.step: Log and remediate plan exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue per missing element, overdue review, stale roster or missed 30-day update with root cause and owner.
Prioritize any gap an OSHA inspection would cite (missing accounting procedure, blocked exit finding) for immediate fix.
Sign off each remediation before closure.
checklist.done: all plan exceptions are tracked, prioritized and closed with Operational Risk Manager sign-off.

checklist.step: Report plan-set health to governance
actions: Report quarterly to the Operational Risk Manager and COO: review completion %, element-gap count, warden coverage, and open exceptions.
Flag any establishment at risk of missing June 30 in the Q2 report by name.
File the reports with the annual evidence.
checklist.done: quarterly reports are issued with at-risk sites named ahead of the deadline.

checklist.step: Retain plan records for five years
actions: File signed plan versions, review records, checklists, warden rosters, PPE certifications and training exports under OSHA/EmergencyPlans/<year>/<establishment>.
Apply the 5-year retention label and preserve superseded versions for the inspection history.
Verify retrieval by establishment and version date.
checklist.done: the plan record set is filed with versions preserved, labelled and retrievable.

checklist.step: Verify readiness for an unannounced OSHA inspection
actions: Annually, run a mock inspection at one establishment: present the EAP, FPP, PPE certifications, warden roster and training records as if to a compliance officer during a walk-around.
Time the assembly of the document set and walk one evacuation route for obstructions and signage.
Log gaps found as tracker issues with the same priority as real citations.
checklist.done: a mock-inspection record exists for the year with all gaps tracked.

testing.step: Tie the tested plan inventory to the establishment register
actions: Pull the establishment register and the GRC plan inventory independently and match one-to-one.
List any covered establishment lacking a plan record or an oral-plan determination as an automatic exception.
Verify oral-plan sites actually had 10 or fewer employees at the determination date using HRIS headcount.
testing.done: the inventory ties to the register and oral-plan headcounts re-verify.

testing.step: Sample plans and re-perform the six-element check
actions: Select the 3 largest establishments plus 5 seeded-random others.
Re-read each sampled EAP against 29 CFR 1910.38(c)(1)-(6) without reference to the analyst's checklist, marking each element independently.
Compare to the recorded checklist; a recorded 'present' the auditor cannot find is an exception.
Repeat for the FPP against 1910.39(c).
testing.done: independent element checks match the recorded checklists or differences are excepted.

testing.step: Verify annual reviews happened by June 30 and were real
actions: Pull GRC review-task completion timestamps for all establishments and flag any after June 30.
For sampled sites, corroborate the review actually occurred: reviewer calendar entries, site-visit records or meeting notes with the office manager.
Treat a task closed with no corroborating trace as an unsupported review.
testing.done: all reviews show on-time timestamps and sampled reviews are corroborated.

testing.step: Walk one site and verify the plan matches reality
actions: At one sampled establishment, walk the primary and secondary evacuation routes against the plan maps, checking exits are unlocked, unobstructed and signed.
Verify the posted maps and assembly-point placard match the current plan version id.
Confirm the printed plan at reception and the intranet copy are the current version.
testing.done: the site walk confirms routes, postings and available copies match the current plan.

testing.step: Verify warden rosters against the HRIS
actions: For sampled sites, match every named warden and critical-operations employee to an active HRIS assignment at that establishment.
Any departed or relocated name still on the roster is an exception with days-stale computed.
Verify quarterly reconciliation records exist for all four quarters.
testing.done: sampled rosters contain only active site employees and quarterly reconciliations exist.

testing.step: Trace move tickets to 30-day plan updates
actions: Pull all facilities move/reconfiguration tickets for the year from ServiceNow.
Match each to a plan-update task and compute ticket-close to plan-version-issue day gaps.
Flag gaps over 30 days and any move with no plan task at all.
Verify retraining triggered for affected employees on sampled updates.
testing.done: every move ticket traces to an in-SLA plan update with retraining evidenced, or is excepted.

testing.step: Verify PPE hazard assessment certifications
actions: Inspect the certification for each exposed role family: workplace identified, certifier signature, assessment dates present per 1910.132(d)(2).
Trace sampled PPE issue records for five exposed employees to the specified equipment.
Check any new role or equipment introduced in the year triggered a re-assessment.
testing.done: certifications are complete, issue records trace, and new-role triggers fired.

testing.step: Test training coverage at the three trigger points
actions: For sampled sites, pull LMS completions and match new hires, responsibility changes and plan-version changes to training events.
Compute coverage rates per trigger type.
List employees past 14 days untrained and unchased as exceptions.
testing.done: trigger-point coverage rates are computed with gaps excepted.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise an issue per exception (element gap, late review, stale warden, missed move update) with root cause and owner.
Prioritize anything citable in an inspection for fix within 15 days.
Set retest flags for next year's test.
testing.done: all exceptions are tracked with priorities, owners and retest flags.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: State results against the thresholds: 100% reviewed plans with all elements, zero stale wardens, all move updates in 30 days.
Write the conclusion with workpaper references and the site-walk findings.
Sign as independent reviewer with Operational Risk Manager countersignature.
File in the compliance evidence repository and report to the COO.
testing.done: a signed conclusion against the thresholds is filed and reported to the COO.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 29 CFR 1910.38 (the EAP the drills exercise), 29 CFR 1910.165 (alarm systems being tested), 1910.157 (extinguisher availability during drills), and OSHA's evacuation-planning guidance, re-read before the annual drill calendar is set; results feed the 1904-recordable intake if a drill injury occurs

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Operating Officer; reviewed annually and after any drill that surfaced a life-safety failure

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: One full evacuation drill per establishment per calendar year, completed by October 31 to leave remediation time; corrective actions closed within 30 days of the drill; alarm systems tested and records kept per the facilities maintenance schedule under 1910.165(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any establishment without a completed drill by October 31, any unaccounted person at assembly, and any corrective action open past 30 days is logged with root cause and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Operational Risk Manager signs off closure of every drill failure and every overdue corrective action

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All establishments on the register and their drill records for the tested year, the notification-tool activation logs, alarm test records, and every corrective action raised from drills
