checklist.step: Publish the annual drill calendar
actions: By January 31, schedule one full evacuation drill per establishment in the GRC module, spread across quarters and avoiding quarter-end financial close weeks.
Coordinate multi-tenant buildings with the landlord's fire-safety officer and align to any building-wide drill the lease mandates.
Name the drill controller, observers and warden briefing date per site.
Publish the calendar to site office managers — withholding exact dates from general staff where a no-notice drill is planned.
checklist.done: every establishment has a scheduled drill with controller and observers named by January 31.

checklist.step: Prepare each drill with a script and observer pack
actions: Prepare the drill script: alarm activation method and time, any simulated blocked exit (rotate yearly to exercise secondary routes), and the stop conditions.
Print the observer pack: route coverage assignments, timing sheet (alarm to last-person-out, alarm to accounting-complete), and behaviour checklist (doors closed, lifts avoided, PPE where required).
Pull the day-of HRIS site roster and the visitor log procedure for the accounting check.
Brief wardens 48 hours ahead without revealing the blocked-exit choice.
checklist.done: each drill has a script, observer pack, roster source and briefed wardens before drill day.

checklist.step: Confirm alarm and notification systems before the drill
actions: Verify with facilities that the fire alarm's last maintenance/test record is current per the 1910.165(d) schedule and the landlord contract.
Pre-stage the mass-notification tool's drill template (distinct from real-emergency wording) and verify the site's contact list refreshed from the HRIS within the month.
Notify the alarm monitoring company of the drill window so the fire service is not dispatched.
Log these confirmations on the drill record.
checklist.done: alarm test currency, notification template and monitoring-company notice are logged pre-drill.

checklist.step: Execute the evacuation drill and time it
actions: Activate the alarm per script and start timing; observers log route usage, blocked-exit rerouting, and any employee remaining at a desk.
Critical-operations staff execute their delay-then-evacuate steps and observers record the delay duration.
Record alarm-to-last-person-out time per floor and total building time on the timing sheet.
Stop the drill on the stop conditions and give the all-clear through the notification tool.
checklist.done: the drill ran per script with timing sheets completed and the all-clear issued.

checklist.step: Run the accounting at the assembly point
actions: Wardens count their zones against the day's HRIS site roster and the reception visitor log at the assembly point.
Resolve every unaccounted name before the drill closes — locate the person or confirm off-site status via their manager; an unresolved name is a drill failure, not a footnote.
Record accounting-complete time and the count reconciliation on the results form.
Note visitors and contractors accounted for separately.
checklist.done: the accounting reconciles to the roster and visitor log with zero unresolved names and times recorded.

checklist.step: Complete the results form the same day
actions: Enter into the GRC drill record: date and time, participation estimate, alarm-to-out and alarm-to-accounted times, observer findings, blocked-exit performance, and any injury (an injury goes to the C01 recordability intake immediately).
Attach the timing sheets, accounting reconciliation and notification-tool activation log.
Grade the drill pass/fail against the procedure's standards (all floors evacuated, accounting complete, no life-safety findings).
Have the site office manager countersign the form.
checklist.done: a same-day, countersigned results form with attachments and a pass/fail grade exists in the GRC record.

checklist.step: Raise corrective actions within 5 days and close within 30
actions: Convert every observer finding into a GRC corrective action within 5 business days: owner, fix, due date within 30 days of the drill.
Route physical fixes (signage, door hardware, obstruction removal) to facilities via ServiceNow and link the ticket.
Route plan-content findings to the REG-055-C05 plan-amendment process.
Escalate to the Operational Risk Manager at day 30 for anything open.
checklist.done: every finding is a corrective action raised in 5 days with linked tickets and 30-day closure tracking.

checklist.step: Run the annual emergency-response tabletop
actions: Once a year, exercise the emergency-response team on a scenario beyond evacuation — medical emergency at a site, severe-weather shelter-in-place, or workplace-violence lockdown (coordinated with the REG-055-C07 programme).
Walk the team through decision points: notification cascade, accounting variant for shelter-in-place, communication to families and media referral to Communications.
Record decisions, gaps and improvement actions on the exercise record with the same 30-day corrective loop.
checklist.done: an annual tabletop record exists with gaps converted to corrective actions.

checklist.step: Test the mass-notification cascade separately
actions: Twice yearly, send a test activation through the notification tool to each establishment's staff list and measure delivery and acknowledgment rates within 30 minutes.
Chase bounced or unreachable contacts through HR to fix stale numbers in the HRIS.
File the activation report with delivery statistics per site.
checklist.done: semi-annual activation reports show delivery rates with stale contacts remediated.

checklist.step: Cover special populations in every drill
actions: Before each drill, identify employees needing evacuation assistance from the confidential accommodations list held by HR, and confirm a buddy and a refuge-area procedure per person.
Verify during the drill that each assistance plan executed, without naming individuals on the general results form.
Update assistance plans for new accommodations within 15 days of HR notice.
checklist.done: every drill evidences executed assistance plans with confidentiality preserved.

checklist.step: Track drill completion against the October 31 deadline
actions: Review the GRC drill dashboard monthly; at the 60-day alert, confirm logistics for every undrilled site.
Rebook any postponed drill within 30 days of postponement — a drill pushed past October 31 needs Operational Risk Manager approval in writing.
Report completion percentage in the quarterly governance report.
checklist.done: the dashboard shows all sites drilled by October 31 or carrying written approval for a later date.

checklist.step: Feed drill outcomes into plan and training updates
actions: Send timing trends and route findings to the REG-055-C05 annual plan review as input evidence.
Trigger LMS retraining for floors that performed poorly (slow response, lift use, desk lingering).
Document the handoff so the drill-to-plan loop is auditable.
checklist.done: drill outputs are evidenced as inputs to plan reviews and targeted retraining.

checklist.step: Log programme exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any missed drill, unresolved accounting name, drill injury, or corrective action past 30 days.
Assign root cause (scheduling failure, warden gap, roster data stale) and an owner.
Sign off closures personally.
checklist.done: programme exceptions are tracked with root cause and signed closures.

checklist.step: Retain drill evidence for five years
actions: File results forms, timing sheets, accounting reconciliations, activation logs, tabletop records and corrective-action closures under OSHA/Drills/<year>/<establishment>.
Apply the 5-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by establishment and drill date.
checklist.done: the year's drill evidence is filed, labelled and retrievable.

checklist.step: Review the programme annually for coverage and realism
actions: Each December, review the year: completion rate, timing trends, repeated findings, and whether scenarios are rotating (blocked exits, no-notice drills, shelter-in-place).
Adjust next year's procedure and calendar accordingly and obtain COO approval.
File the annual programme review note.
checklist.done: an approved annual programme review sets next year's calendar and scenario rotation.

testing.step: Tie drill records to the establishment register
actions: Pull the establishment register and the GRC drill records for the year and match one drill per site.
List any undrilled establishment, or one drilled after October 31 without written Operational Risk Manager approval, as an exception.
Record the completion rate in the workpaper.
testing.done: every establishment matches a completed drill or is excepted with the approval status noted.

testing.step: Inspect results forms for contemporaneity and completeness
actions: Sample 8 establishments (3 largest + 5 seeded-random) and inspect each results form for same-day completion (GRC record timestamps versus drill date), timing entries, countersignature and pass/fail grade.
Treat a form created more than 5 days after the drill date as non-contemporaneous — grade the drill as unevidenced.
Verify attachments (timing sheet, accounting reconciliation) are present, not placeholders.
testing.done: sampled forms are contemporaneous and complete or the drill is graded unevidenced.

testing.step: Corroborate drills against independent system logs
actions: For each sampled drill, pull the notification-tool activation log and the building alarm-panel event log (via facilities or the landlord) for the drill date and time.
Confirm the alarm event and activation timestamps bracket the recorded drill times.
A drill record with no corroborating alarm or activation log entry is an exception — paper drills are findings, not drills.
testing.done: every sampled drill is corroborated by at least one independent system log.

testing.step: Re-verify the accounting reconciliation
actions: For 3 sampled drills, re-pull the drill-day HRIS site roster and compare to the accounting sheet totals.
Verify every unaccounted name shows a same-day resolution note.
Check visitors were accounted from the reception log, not estimated.
testing.done: accounting sheets reconcile to day-of rosters with all resolutions documented.

testing.step: Trace corrective actions to closure within 30 days
actions: Pull every corrective action raised from the year's drills with raised and closed dates.
Compute the 30-day closure rate against the ≥90% threshold.
For 5 sampled physical fixes, verify the linked ServiceNow ticket shows the work done (photos, completion notes), not just the GRC action closed.
Check plan-content findings actually reached the C05 amendment process.
testing.done: the closure rate is computed and sampled fixes verify as physically done and plan findings as handed off.

testing.step: Verify special-population coverage
actions: With HR, confirm the count of active evacuation-assistance accommodations per sampled site (names withheld).
Verify each sampled drill record evidences that count of assistance plans executed.
Confirm no individual is named on general drill forms.
testing.done: assistance-plan execution counts match accommodation counts with confidentiality intact.

testing.step: Verify tabletop and notification tests occurred
actions: Inspect the annual tabletop record for scenario, attendee list, decisions and corrective actions.
Inspect both semi-annual notification-test reports and their delivery rates; verify stale-contact remediation happened by re-checking a sample against the HRIS.
List a missing tabletop or notification test as an exception.
testing.done: the tabletop and both notification tests are evidenced with remediation verified.

testing.step: Recompute timing standards and injury handling
actions: Compare sampled drill evacuation times to the procedure's standards and confirm fails were graded fails.
For any drill injury recorded, trace it to a C01 recordability determination within 7 days.
Verify the monitoring-company pre-notice exists for each sampled drill (no false dispatches).
testing.done: grades match the standards, drill injuries traced to recordkeeping, and pre-notices exist.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise an issue per exception (missed drill, unevidenced drill, failed corroboration, open corrective action) with root cause and owner.
Escalate any paper-drill finding to the Operational Risk Manager and COO as an integrity issue.
Set remediation dates and next-cycle retest flags.
testing.done: all exceptions are tracked with escalations and retest flags set.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: State results against the thresholds: 100% drilled, zero unresolved accounting names, ≥90% 30-day closures.
Write the conclusion with workpaper references including the corroboration results.
Sign as independent reviewer (organized/observed no tested drill) with Operational Risk Manager countersignature.
File the workpaper and report to the COO and Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed conclusion against all thresholds is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Define the register schema and recognized-hazard settings
actions: Configure the GRC register with fields: hazard description, setting (branch reception, field adjusting, SIU investigation, premium audit, cash handling, lone/after-hours work, contractor on-site), exposed population and headcount, likelihood/severity rating, current controls, control owner, last review date, next review date.
Seed the settings list from OSHA's workplace-violence risk-factor guidance: public contact, exchange of money, mobile workplace, working alone or late, and working in high-crime areas.
Record the schema decision note and obtain Operational Risk Manager approval.
Set the anniversary-review workflow on every entry.
checklist.done: the register schema is live in the GRC with approved settings and anniversary workflows armed.

checklist.step: Assess workplace-violence exposure per setting
actions: For each setting, interview the managing role (Claims Director for field adjusters, SIU Manager for investigators, Contact Center Ops Manager for walk-in locations) about actual encounters, near-misses and aggravating factors.
Pull the last three years of ER cases tagged 'threat/violence' and map them to settings.
Rate likelihood and severity per setting using the program's matrix and write the exposed-population headcount from the HRIS.
Enter one register row per distinct hazard-setting pair — 'field adjuster meets hostile claimant at loss site' and 'SIU investigator confronts fraud suspect' are separate rows with separate controls.
checklist.done: every setting has assessed, rated register rows grounded in interviews and three years of case data.

checklist.step: Attach feasible abatement controls to every hazard row
actions: For each row, document the controls in the register: e.g. two-person visits for threat-flagged claims, lone-worker check-in app with escalation, reception panic buttons and layout barriers, de-escalation training, cash-handling limits and drops, after-hours access controls.
Name a control owner per control and the evidence each control produces (check-in logs, training exports, panic-button test records).
A hazard row with no feasible control documented is a program failure — escalate it to the Operational Risk Manager rather than leave it blank.
Version the register on every control change.
checklist.done: every register row carries named, owned controls with defined evidence, or an escalated gap.

checklist.step: Stand up the threat reporting and response procedure
actions: Publish the reporting channel: any employee reports threats, aggression or violence through the ER case tool or the emergency line, with no-retaliation wording consistent with REG-055-C04.

Define the response tiers: imminent risk — call police first, then the response team; credible threat — same-day threat-assessment huddle (ER, Security, Employment Counsel, the manager); other — 3-business-day assessment.
Auto-open a register-update task with a 30-day SLA on every 'threat/violence' tag.
Test the intake path quarterly with a scripted scenario.
checklist.done: the reporting channel, tiered response and register-update automation are live and quarterly-tested.

checklist.step: Operate the lone-worker check-in protocol for field roles
actions: Require field claims adjusters, SIU field investigators and premium auditors to log each field visit in the check-in app: address, expected duration, and check-out confirmation.
Configure escalation: missed check-out triggers an automated call, then supervisor contact, then police welfare check per the timing table.
Flag threat-marked claims/accounts in the claims platform so a two-person visit or office-only meeting is enforced before dispatch.
Review check-in compliance monthly per team and coach gaps.
checklist.done: field visits are logged with working escalation and threat-flag enforcement, reviewed monthly.

checklist.step: Exchange hazard information with on-site contractors and vendors
actions: For every vendor working on premises (cleaning, security, facilities trades, catering), exchange hazard information both ways per the multi-employer worksite policy: give them the site EAP and hazard summary; obtain their activity hazards and controls.
Record the exchange in the procurement contract file and link it from the register's contractor rows.
Require vendor incidents on site to be reported to the company within 24 hours via the contract clause.
Refresh the exchange at contract renewal or on scope change.
checklist.done: every on-site vendor has a documented two-way hazard exchange linked to the register.

checklist.step: Deliver de-escalation and violence-prevention training
actions: Assign role-based modules: de-escalation and exit strategies for customer-facing and field staff; threat-recognition and response for managers; reception-specific procedures for front-desk staff.
Set completion within 30 days of assignment to an exposed role and refresh every 24 months.
Build scenarios from anonymized company incidents.
Export completions to the register's control evidence.
checklist.done: exposed-role training coverage is current within the 24-month refresh with exports linked to the register.

checklist.step: Review every register entry on its anniversary
actions: Work the GRC anniversary task: re-interview the setting owner, re-check incident data since last review, and re-rate likelihood/severity.
Verify each control's evidence actually exists for the period (spot-open the check-in logs, training exports, panic-button test records).
Update or retire the row with a reviewer note; retired hazards keep their history.
Escalate any row that cannot complete review within 14 days of anniversary.
checklist.done: every register row shows an anniversary review with re-rating and evidenced controls.

checklist.step: Update the register within 30 days of every incident
actions: On each 'threat/violence' case closure, determine whether it reveals a new hazard, a control failure, or a likelihood change.
Amend the affected register rows within 30 days, citing the case id.
Where the incident caused a recordable injury, confirm the C01 log entry and, if hospitalization occurred, the C08 report were made.
Close the auto-opened register-update task with the amendment reference.
checklist.done: every incident case links to a register amendment (or documented no-change) within 30 days.

checklist.step: Test physical controls on a schedule
actions: Test reception panic buttons monthly with the monitoring vendor and log the result.
Verify after-hours badge restrictions quarterly with an access-report review from the IAM platform.
Walk reception layouts annually for barrier and egress adequacy.
File test results as control evidence on the register rows.
checklist.done: panic-button, access-control and layout tests are logged on schedule against their register rows.

checklist.step: Run an annual program review with leadership
actions: Compile the annual picture: incident counts by setting, register changes, control test results, training coverage and open actions.
Present to the Chief HR Officer and Operational Risk Manager with recommended program changes.
Record decisions and update the program document within 30 days.
checklist.done: the annual review is presented and decided changes land in the program document within 30 days.

checklist.step: Maintain the OSHA-inquiry evidence pack
actions: Keep an assembled pack: program document, current register export, training coverage report, control test summaries and the incident-response procedure — the material that answers a General Duty Clause recognized-hazard-and-feasible-abatement inquiry.
Refresh the pack quarterly and after any significant incident.
Time an assembly drill annually against the five-business-day response standard.
checklist.done: a quarterly-refreshed evidence pack exists and the assembly drill met five business days.

checklist.step: Log register exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any overdue anniversary review, missed 30-day incident update, failed control test or training gap in an exposed role.
Assign root cause and owner; prioritize control failures over documentation lag.
Sign off closures personally.
checklist.done: register exceptions are tracked with root cause and signed closures.

checklist.step: Restrict and retain threat-case records properly
actions: File register versions, assessments, control evidence and program reviews under OSHA/ViolencePrevention/<year> with 5-year retention.
Hold threat-case files in a restricted folder limited to ER, Security leadership and Employment Counsel.
Verify retrieval by setting, establishment and case id.
checklist.done: records are retained 5 years with threat files access-restricted and retrievable.

checklist.step: Coordinate the lockdown scenario with the drill programme
actions: Include a workplace-violence lockdown or shelter-in-place scenario in the REG-055-C06 tabletop rotation at least every two years.
Feed exercise findings back into the register's control rows and the response procedure.
Document the cross-reference in both programmes' records.
checklist.done: the lockdown scenario appears in the exercise rotation with findings fed to the register.

testing.step: Verify register completeness against independent sources
actions: Export the full register and reconcile settings coverage against the HRIS role catalogue for exposed roles (field adjusters, SIU, premium audit, reception, cash handling) and against the procurement list of on-site vendors.
List any exposed role or on-site vendor population with no register row as an exception.
Verify every row has a control, an owner and a next-review date — blanks are automatic fails.
testing.done: the register covers all exposed populations and vendors with no blank controls.

testing.step: Test anniversary-review currency
actions: Compute months-since-review for every register row and flag any over 12 months.
For 8 sampled rows, corroborate the review happened: interview notes, evidence spot-checks recorded, re-rating rationale.
Treat a review task closed with no notes as unsupported.
testing.done: all rows are inside 12 months and sampled reviews are corroborated.

testing.step: Trace incidents to register updates
actions: Pull all ER cases tagged 'threat/violence' closed in the year.
Match each to a register amendment or documented no-change decision and compute the day gap against the 30-day SLA.
Verify recordable-injury incidents also trace to a C01 log entry and, where hospitalization occurred, a C08 report.
Search two sample months of ER cases for violence keywords to catch untagged incidents missing from the population.
testing.done: every incident traces to a timely register decision and the tag population is proven complete.

testing.step: Re-perform one setting assessment
actions: Pick the highest-rated setting and independently re-assess: interview the managing role and two exposed employees, review the case history, and re-rate likelihood/severity.
Compare to the register rating; a materially lower auditor rating suggests stale optimism — challenge it with the Operational Risk Manager.
Document the re-assessment note.
testing.done: an independent re-assessment exists with any rating divergence challenged and resolved.

testing.step: Sample lone-worker check-in compliance
actions: Pull the claims platform's field-visit records for a sample month and match each visit to a check-in app entry with check-out.
Compute the check-in compliance rate and list threat-flagged claims visited without the two-person control — each is an automatic fail.
Test the escalation chain once: trigger a controlled missed check-out and time the automated call and supervisor contact.
testing.done: check-in compliance is computed, two-person control breaches listed, and the escalation chain fired correctly.

testing.step: Verify contractor hazard exchanges
actions: Sample 5 on-site vendor contracts from procurement and inspect the two-way hazard-exchange documents and the 24-hour incident-reporting clause.
Verify the exchange is linked from the register's contractor rows and refreshed at the last renewal.
List any on-site vendor with no exchange as an exception.
testing.done: sampled vendor files show current two-way exchanges linked to the register.

testing.step: Re-perform control tests
actions: Witness a panic-button test at one reception site and compare to the monthly log history for gaps.
Re-run the after-hours access report from the IAM platform for one quarter and compare to the recorded quarterly review.
Pull the LMS export and compute exposed-role training currency against the 24-month refresh rule.
testing.done: witnessed and re-run control tests match the logged evidence and training currency is computed.

testing.step: Inspect threat-case handling against the tiers
actions: For 5 sampled threat cases, verify the response tier applied matches the facts (imminent → police-first same day; credible → same-day huddle with counsel present).
Check huddle attendance and decisions are minuted and access-restricted.
Confirm no case file sits outside the restricted folder.
testing.done: sampled cases show correct tiering, minuted decisions and restricted storage.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise an issue per exception (coverage gap, stale review, missed incident update, control breach) with root cause and owner.
Escalate two-person-control breaches and untagged incidents to the CHRO and Operational Risk Manager immediately.
Set remediation dates and next-cycle retests.
testing.done: all exceptions are tracked with escalations made and retests armed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: State results against the thresholds: 100% review currency, 100% incident updates in 30 days, zero uncontrolled field visits to flagged accounts.
Write the conclusion with workpaper references, noting the General Duty Clause posture — a recognized hazard with an unevidenced control is the finding that matters most.
Sign as independent reviewer with Operational Risk Manager countersignature.
File the workpaper and report to the CHRO and Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed conclusion against the thresholds is filed and reported to governance.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the 29 CFR 1904.39 severe-event reporting duty — fatality within 8 hours, in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours — with a 24/7 on-call rota; escalation to the Chief HR Officer and Employment Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 29 CFR 1904.39(a)(1)-(3) (report clocks and channels), 1904.39(b) (reporting window rules: fatality reportable if within 30 days of the incident, hospitalization/amputation/eye loss if within 24 hours of the incident) and the underlying 1904.7 recordability duty, re-read at each rota briefing

In-scope processes.value: 24/7 intake of severe workplace events at any establishment or field location → confirmation of reportability and clock computation → report to OSHA by phone (1-800-321-OSHA), the nearest area office, or the online Serious Event Reporting Application → follow-up, Rapid Response Investigation handling and log entry

In-scope systems.value: Severe-event tickets with clock timestamps run in the workflow/case management tool; the OSHA report itself goes by phone to 1-800-321-6742 or via the Serious Event Reporting Application at osha.gov; evidence in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Severe Event Reporting Procedure — event definitions (in-patient hospitalization means formal admission to in-patient service, not ER observation; amputation includes fingertip loss with or without bone), clock computation from employer knowledge, the three permitted report channels, required report content (establishment name, location and time of incident, number and names of affected employees, contact person, brief description), state-plan office variations, and the no-delegation rule that reporting waits for no investigation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief HR Officer with Employment Counsel concurrence; reviewed annually and after every actual report or near-miss of a deadline

In-patient hospitalization, amputation, loss of an eye: within 24 hours of knowledge (reportable if within 24 hours of the incident). Clocks run from when any agent or employee of the employer learns of the event

Deadline reminders configured.value: The severe-event ticket type stamps the knowledge time at creation and displays a live countdown; the on-call phone tree alerts the HR Operations Manager, Employment Counsel and CHRO simultaneously; a 4-hour-remaining alarm fires to the backup reporter

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Severe-event tickets with knowledge and report timestamps, the OSHA confirmation (call reference or application submission receipt), Rapid Response Investigation correspondence and the linked Form 300 entry, retained 5 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any report made after the 8/24-hour clock, any severe event discovered unreported, and any drill failure of the on-call chain is logged with elapsed-time facts, root cause and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Employment Counsel signs off the handling of every late or missed report — including any decision about voluntary disclosure to the area office — before the exception closes

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All severe-event tickets in the year, every OSHA report made, all hospital-admission and death indicators from WC claims and ER cases (to catch unreported qualifying events), and the quarterly on-call drill records

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of qualifying events reported inside the 8/24-hour clocks; zero qualifying events found in WC/ER data without a report; every actual report followed by a Form 300 entry within 7 days; quarterly drills completing the mock report inside 2 hours

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have made or advised on any tested report and must not sit on the on-call rota

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual severe-event reporting test workpaper (population reconciliation, clock recomputation, channel verification, drill review) in the compliance evidence repository under OSHA/SevereEvents/<year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-event ticket with knowledge timestamp, report confirmation reference, Rapid Response Investigation response letter and abatement evidence, producible within four business hours per 29 CFR 1904.40

Regulator response path.value: After any report, the OSHA area office response (Rapid Response Investigation letter or inspection) routes to Employment Counsel, who owns the written response and any abatement certification; the HR Operations Manager supplies event facts and the C01 records

checklist.step: Maintain the 24/7 on-call reporting rota
actions: Publish a rota of trained reporters (primary and backup per week) with phone numbers, covering nights, weekends and holidays — the 8-hour fatality clock does not pause outside business hours.
Store the rota on the HR intranet emergency page and in the contact center's escalation script so a call reaching any company number can find the reporter.
Brief every rota member on the procedure at onboarding to the rota and annually.
Update the rota within 1 business day of any personnel change.
checklist.done: a current 24/7 rota with briefed reporters is published and reachable through every intake channel.

checklist.step: Wire severe-event intake into every channel where knowledge arrives
actions: Instruct managers, site office managers, the contact center and the security desk: any death, hospital admission, amputation or eye-loss connected to work triggers an immediate call to the on-call reporter — knowledge by any supervisor starts the clock under 1904.39(a).
Configure the WC claim intake and ER case tool so 'fatality' or 'hospitalization' selections auto-page the on-call reporter.
Cover field events: adjusters and field staff carry the reporting card with the on-call number.
Test each channel quarterly as part of the drill.
checklist.done: all intake channels page the on-call reporter automatically or by scripted instruction, tested quarterly.

checklist.step: Open the severe-event ticket and stamp the knowledge time
actions: Open a severe-event ticket immediately on notification, recording: event type, employee(s) affected, establishment or field location, incident date/time, and — critically — the earliest time any employer agent learned of the event, with the source of that knowledge.
Let the ticket compute the deadline: knowledge time + 8 hours (fatality) or + 24 hours (hospitalization/amputation/eye loss).
Never wait for confirmation of medical details to open the ticket — open on report, refine later.
Page Employment Counsel and the CHRO from the ticket.
checklist.done: the ticket exists with a sourced knowledge timestamp and a computed statutory deadline.

checklist.step: Confirm the event qualifies under the 1904.39 definitions
actions: Apply the definitions: in-patient hospitalization means formal admission to the in-patient service — ER treatment or observation alone does not qualify; amputation includes fingertip loss with or without bone but excludes avulsions and lacerations; verify eye loss versus eye injury.

Apply the window rules in 1904.39(b)(6): hospitalization/amputation/eye loss is reportable only if it occurs within 24 hours of the work-related incident; a fatality is reportable if it occurs within 30 days of the incident.

Apply the work-relatedness screen (motor-vehicle accident on a public street outside a work zone and commercial-transport accidents are not phone-reportable, per 1904.39(b)(3)-(4), though still recordable).
Call the hospital or family contact to confirm admission status when unclear — and if still unclear as the clock runs down, report anyway; over-reporting is recoverable, late reporting is not.
Write the qualification rationale on the ticket.
checklist.done: the ticket carries a written qualification call under the definitions and window rules.

checklist.step: Assemble the required report content
actions: Collect the 1904.39(c)(2) content: establishment name, location of the incident, time of the incident, type of reportable event, number of employees affected, their names, the company contact person and phone, and a brief description of the incident.
Confirm the employer of record for any temporary or leased worker with HR — the supervising employer reports.
Have Employment Counsel review the brief description wording where liability facts are sensitive — but never at the cost of the clock.
Stage the content on the ticket for the reporter.
checklist.done: all eight content elements are staged on the ticket, counsel-checked where time allowed.

checklist.step: Make the report through a permitted channel inside the clock
actions: Report by one of the three permitted channels under 1904.39(a)(3): call the OSHA 24-hour central line at 1-800-321-OSHA (6742); call the nearest OSHA area office during business hours; or submit through the online Serious Event Reporting Application on osha.gov.
For establishments in State Plan states, report to the state agency's designated number/portal — keep the state-office contact sheet current on the intranet emergency page.
Record on the ticket: channel used, submission time, the name of the OSHA officer or the application confirmation number.
If the online application fails or is ambiguous close to the deadline, switch to the 800 number — the phone call is always available.
checklist.done: the report is made inside the 8/24-hour clock with channel, time and confirmation reference on the ticket.

checklist.step: Notify internal stakeholders and start the parallel workstreams
actions: After reporting, notify the COO, the establishment leader and Communications (media calls route to Communications only).
Trigger the incident investigation under the safety programme and a litigation hold via Employment Counsel.
Coordinate employee support: manager briefing, EAP referral for witnesses.
Keep the reporting ticket separate from the investigation file — the report could not and did not wait for investigation findings.
checklist.done: stakeholders are notified, the hold and investigation are opened, and the ticket remains a clean reporting record.

checklist.step: Enter the event on the Form 300 log within 7 days
actions: Record the case on the establishment's Form 300 and complete the Form 301 within 7 calendar days under the REG-055-C01 process.
Cross-reference the OSHA report confirmation number on the HRIS case and the log worksheet.
Update day counts and classification as the employee's condition evolves.
checklist.done: the 300/301 entries exist within 7 days and cross-reference the report confirmation.

checklist.step: Handle the OSHA Rapid Response Investigation or inspection
actions: On receiving a Rapid Response Investigation (RRI) letter from the area office, calendar the response deadline (typically 5 business days for the initial response) and own the written submission.
Complete the RRI package with the HR Operations Manager: incident findings, root cause, corrective actions taken and their evidence (photos, work orders, training records).
If OSHA elects an on-site inspection instead, run the inspection protocol: verify credentials, opening conference, accompanied walk-around, document requests through counsel.
File all correspondence on the ticket.
checklist.done: the RRI response or inspection is handled on time with corrective-action evidence filed on the ticket.

checklist.step: Sweep for unreported qualifying events weekly
actions: Each week, screen new WC claims and ER cases for hospital-admission, amputation, eye-loss and death indicators.
Match each hit to a severe-event ticket; for any unmatched hit, page the on-call reporter immediately — a late report now beats a discovered failure later.
Apply the 1904.39(b)(7)-(8) late-knowledge rules: when the employer learns of a qualifying event after the fact, the clock runs from that knowledge.
Log the weekly sweep result even when clean.
checklist.done: the weekly sweep is logged with every indicator matched to a ticket or escalated same-day.

checklist.step: Drill the reporting chain quarterly
actions: Each quarter, run a no-notice mock event through a rotating intake channel (contact center, site manager, WC intake) at an awkward hour.
Time the chain: intake to on-call page, page to ticket, ticket to mock-report-ready, targeting under 2 hours end-to-end.
Stop short of contacting OSHA; the drill ends at a completed mock report reviewed against the content checklist.
Log timings and fix any broken link within 15 days.
checklist.done: four quarterly drill logs per year show the chain completing inside 2 hours or fixes within 15 days.

checklist.step: Keep the state-plan contact sheet and definitions current
actions: Quarterly, verify the reporting number/portal for each State Plan state where the company has establishments or field operations, from the state agency sites.
Watch for 1904.39 amendments and interpretation letters; update the procedure within 30 days of any change.
Date-stamp the contact sheet on each verification.
checklist.done: the contact sheet carries a current-quarter verification stamp and the procedure reflects current rules.

checklist.step: Log any late or missed report as a priority exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue the same day a late or missed report is identified, with the elapsed-time facts and how it was discovered.
Have Employment Counsel assess exposure (citation risk for failure to report) and decide the voluntary-disclosure posture with the area office.
Assign root cause (knowledge not escalated, definition misread, rota gap) and fix the failing link within 15 days.
Close only with counsel sign-off.
checklist.done: every late/missed report shows a same-day issue, counsel assessment, fixed root cause and signed closure.

checklist.step: Retain the severe-event evidence
actions: File each event's ticket, report confirmation, RRI correspondence and corrective-action evidence under OSHA/SevereEvents/<year>/<event-id> with 5-year retention.
Link the record to the establishment's C01 log entry.
Verify four-business-hour retrievability as part of the C01 drill rotation.
checklist.done: each event's full record is filed, linked to the log, and retrievable within four business hours.

checklist.step: Brief leadership after every actual event
actions: Within 10 business days of any actual report, debrief the CHRO, COO and Compliance Officer: timeline achieved versus the clock, what OSHA did, corrective actions and any procedure change needed.
Feed hazard findings into the REG-055-C07 register and the C05 plan set where relevant.
File the debrief note with the event record.
checklist.done: a debrief note within 10 business days links the event to procedure and register updates.

testing.step: Build the qualifying-event population independently
actions: Extract from WC claims, ER cases and the Form 300 logs every death, in-patient hospitalization, amputation and eye-loss indicator for the year — independent of the severe-event tickets.
Pull all severe-event tickets and all OSHA report confirmations for the same period.
Record counts of each set in the workpaper before matching.
testing.done: independent indicator, ticket and report populations are extracted and counted.

testing.step: Reconcile indicators to tickets and reports
actions: Match every indicator to a ticket and every qualifying ticket to an OSHA report confirmation.
For unmatched indicators, re-perform the qualification call (admission vs observation, the 24-hour/30-day window rules, work-relatedness exceptions) and classify as correctly-not-reported or missed.
Any missed qualifying event is an automatic fail escalated to Employment Counsel during fieldwork, not at report issuance.
testing.done: every indicator is matched or classified, with missed events escalated immediately.

testing.step: Recompute the clock on every actual report
actions: For each reported event, take the earliest employer-knowledge evidence (first call log, page timestamp, email) rather than the ticket's asserted knowledge time.
Recompute elapsed time from earliest knowledge to the report submission time and compare to the 8- or 24-hour limit.
Flag any ticket whose stamped knowledge time post-dates evidence of earlier supervisor knowledge — clock manipulation is a severity-one finding.
Document the timeline per event in the workpaper.
testing.done: every report has a recomputed elapsed time from evidence-based knowledge, with discrepancies flagged.

testing.step: Verify report channel and content
actions: For each report, verify the confirmation artifact: 800-number call reference with officer name, area-office call note, or Serious Event Reporting Application receipt.
Check the staged content covered all eight 1904.39(c)(2) elements.
For State Plan establishments, verify the report went to the correct state channel per the contact sheet in force that day.
testing.done: every report shows a valid confirmation, complete content and the correct federal/state channel.

testing.step: Trace reports to Form 300 entries and RRI responses
actions: Trace each reported event to its Form 300/301 entry within 7 days and the cross-referenced confirmation number.
Inspect RRI correspondence for on-time responses and evidence-backed corrective actions.
Verify the litigation hold issued and the investigation file is separate from the reporting ticket.
testing.done: every event traces through log entry, RRI handling and hold with clean separation.

testing.step: Test the weekly sweep operation
actions: Pull the year's weekly sweep logs and verify a log exists for every week including holidays.
Re-run the sweep query for two sample months and compare hits to the logged results.
Verify any sweep-discovered event shows a same-day page and a late-knowledge clock start per 1904.39(b)(7).
testing.done: sweep logs are complete, re-runs match, and discovered events show correct late-knowledge handling.

testing.step: Review the quarterly drills and rota integrity
actions: Inspect all four drill logs: channel rotated, off-hours timing used, end-to-end time against the 2-hour target, fixes closed within 15 days.
Check the rota had no coverage gaps by sampling four holiday/weekend dates and confirming a named, briefed reporter was assigned.
Call the on-call number once, unannounced, during fieldwork and verify a reporter answers or returns within the procedure's response time.
testing.done: drills ran quarterly with fixes closed, the rota shows no gaps, and the live call test passed.

testing.step: Re-perform qualification calls on edge cases
actions: Select every event classified as not-reportable on definitional grounds (ER-only treatment, motor-vehicle exception, outside the 24-hour window).
Re-perform each call against 1904.39(b) with the medical and timeline evidence on file.
Route disagreements to Employment Counsel for a ruling; a wrong not-reportable call is a missed report.
testing.done: every definitional exclusion is independently re-performed with disagreements ruled by counsel.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise an issue per exception (missed report, late report, clock manipulation, drill gap, sweep miss) with root cause and owner.
Confirm counsel's exposure assessment and disclosure decision is attached for any missed/late report.
Set remediation dates and next-cycle retests; missed-report root causes get a 15-day fix deadline.
testing.done: all exceptions are tracked with counsel assessments attached and fixes deadlined.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: State results against the thresholds: 100% on-time reports, zero swept-up misses, log entries within 7 days, drills inside 2 hours.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the per-event timeline evidence referenced.
Sign as independent reviewer (not on the rota, advised on no report) with Compliance Officer countersignature.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report to the CHRO, COO and Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed conclusion against all thresholds is filed and reported to governance.
